name: Read a scale between marked units
description: Student can read a measurement at a point between the marked units on a scaled instrument.
exampleOfSuccess: On a jug marked every 100 mL, the student reads a level as 250 mL.
commonError: Student reads only the marked numbers, rounding to the nearest mark.
checkpointTask: Give scaled instruments with values between marks. Ask the student to read each.

name: Choose the unit and instrument
description: Student can choose a suitable unit and instrument to measure an attribute.
exampleOfSuccess: To measure a desk, the student chooses a tape measure and centimetres.
commonError: Student chooses an instrument or unit that does not suit the attribute.
checkpointTask: Name things to measure. Ask the student which instrument and unit they would use.

name: Measure mass with scales
description: Student can measure mass using digital or analog kitchen scales.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads a parcel as 350 g on the scales.
commonError: Student misreads between the markings or the digital display.
checkpointTask: Give objects and scales. Ask the student to measure the mass of each.

name: Measure capacity with a jug
description: Student can measure capacity using a scaled measuring jug.
exampleOfSuccess: The student measures 600 mL of water in the jug.
commonError: Student reads the level above or below eye line, misreading the scale.
checkpointTask: Give a jug and containers. Ask the student to measure the capacity of each.

name: Read temperature on a scale
description: Student can read temperature on a scaled thermometer.
exampleOfSuccess: The student reads 22 degrees between the marked tens.
commonError: Student reads only the marked numbers or misreads the scale direction.
checkpointTask: Show thermometers at various readings. Ask the student to read each.

name: Find the perimeter of a shape
description: Student can find the perimeter of a shape by adding the side lengths.
exampleOfSuccess: For a rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm, the student adds the four sides to get 16 cm.
commonError: Student adds only two sides, or confuses perimeter with area.
checkpointTask: Give shapes with labelled sides. Ask the student to find the perimeter.

name: Measure area by counting units
description: Student can find the area of a shape by counting square units.
exampleOfSuccess: On grid paper, the student counts the squares a rectangle covers.
commonError: Student counts the boundary squares only, or counts unit lengths.
checkpointTask: Give shapes on grid paper. Ask the student to find the area in square units.

name: Distinguish area from perimeter
description: Student can distinguish between area and perimeter and choose the right one for a task.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked how much fence is needed, the student chooses perimeter; for turf, area.
commonError: Student uses area when perimeter is needed, or the reverse.
checkpointTask: Pose tasks. Ask the student whether each needs area or perimeter and why.

name: Approximate the area of an irregular shape
description: Student can approximate the area of an irregular shape using square units.
exampleOfSuccess: Counting whole and part squares, the student estimates the area of a leaf shape.
commonError: Student ignores part squares, or counts every touched square as whole.
checkpointTask: Give an irregular shape on grid paper. Ask the student to approximate its area.

name: Calculate elapsed time
description: Student can calculate the amount of time between two events.
exampleOfSuccess: From 9:15 to 9:50, the student finds 35 minutes.
commonError: Student subtracts the digits without regard to 60 minutes in an hour.
checkpointTask: Pose start and end times. Ask the student to find the elapsed time.

name: Use am and pm
description: Student can use am and pm to describe and reason about times.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 3 pm is in the afternoon and 3 am is at night.
commonError: Student confuses am and pm, or thinks 12 pm is midnight.
checkpointTask: Pose times. Ask the student to use am or pm and reason about them.

name: Convert between units of time
description: Student can convert between units of time using known relationships.
exampleOfSuccess: The student converts 120 minutes to 2 hours.
checkpointTask: Pose conversions between minutes, hours and days. Ask the student to convert each.

name: Solve a duration problem across am and pm
description: Student can solve a duration problem that crosses from am to pm.
exampleOfSuccess: From 11:30 am to 1:15 pm, the student finds 1 hour 45 minutes.
commonError: Student miscounts across the midday boundary.
checkpointTask: Pose duration problems that cross midday. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Name types of angles
description: Student can name angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex or a revolution.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown an angle smaller than a right angle, the student calls it acute.
commonError: Student confuses acute and obtuse, or calls any angle a right angle.
checkpointTask: Show angles of different sizes. Ask the student to name each type.

name: Compare an angle to a right angle
description: Student can compare an angle to a right angle and name it accordingly.
exampleOfSuccess: Using a right-angle template, the student decides an angle is obtuse.
commonError: Student compares by arm length rather than the opening.
checkpointTask: Give angles and a right-angle template. Ask the student to compare and name each.

name: Estimate the size of an angle
description: Student can estimate whether an angle is acute, right or obtuse before checking.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates an angle as obtuse, then checks with a template.
commonError: Student estimates by appearance with no reference to a right angle.
checkpointTask: Show angles. Ask the student to estimate the type before checking.

name: Classify the angles in a shape
description: Student can classify the interior angles of a shape by type.
exampleOfSuccess: In a triangle, the student identifies the acute and the obtuse angles.
commonError: Student labels all angles the same, or misjudges the right angle.
checkpointTask: Give shapes. Ask the student to classify each interior angle.
